name: tafsir-library
description:
Thirteen classical works of Qur'anic exegesis (tafsir) in their original Arabic, in order of their authors' deaths: al-Tabari, al-Maturidi, al-Zamakhshari, Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, al-Qurtubi, al-Baydawi, al-Nasafi, Ibn Kathir, al-Jalalayn, al-Suyuti's al-Durr al-Manthur, Abu al-Su'ud, Isma'il Haqqi Bursawi and al-Alusi: about 552,000 sentences, together with the Qur'an's text.

Each work is divided into verse units and every sentence has a stable address:
- Ask about a verse and see, work by work, the unit that treats it and the sentences that quote it.
- Search by the works' own Arabic words or by meaning in any language.
- Read a unit or a passage in context and quote it exactly, with a numbered list of sources checked against the text.

Each work belongs to its author: editors' introductions are a separate layer, and two exegetes treating the same verse is never presented as one following another unless a link is recorded. ChatGPT's own translations are labelled as AI translations, and nothing ChatGPT writes is called tafsir.

The texts come from OpenITI (KITAB project; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), each in its chosen edition; the Qur'an's text from the Tanzil Project. All tools are read-only and work without an account. A volunteer, non-commercial project.

defaultPrompt: Zemahşerî ve Beyzâvî, Fâtiha 1:5'teki «iyyâke na'büdü» hakkında ne diyor? Kaynaklarıyla alıntıla.
Go through the exegetes on Ayat al-Kursi (al-Baqara 2:255) in order of their deaths, one key point each.
Which exegetes explain why the Qur'an uses parables, and how?

positive.description: Compares two exegetes on a verse with exact quotations.
positive.prompt: What do al-Zamakhshari and al-Baydawi say about 'iyyaka na'budu' (al-Fatiha 1:5)? Quote them with sources.
positive.expected_behavior: find_ayah gives each work's unit for 1:5; the assistant reads al-Kashshaf's and Anwar al-Tanzil's units, quotes each in Arabic exactly with its own translation labelled as an AI translation, keeps the two apart and ends with a numbered Sources list.

positive.description: Surveys the exegetes on a verse in order of their authors' deaths.
positive.prompt: Go through the exegetes on Ayat al-Kursi (al-Baqara 2:255) in order of their deaths, one key point each.
positive.expected_behavior: Uses find_ayah's list (al-Tabari first, al-Alusi last), names the Risale-i Nur places tied to the verse first, by citation only, and gives one quoted point from each work it reads, each with its source; does not present one exegete as following another.

positive.description: Searches the works by their own Arabic words.
positive.prompt: Search the works for 'الحروف المقطعة' and show where it is discussed.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns sentences from several works with the phrase, reads some in context and quotes them exactly with their sources.

positive.description: Finds a discussion by meaning across the works.
positive.prompt: Which exegetes explain why the Qur'an uses parables, and how?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds passages on the purpose of the Qur'an's parables in more than one work, quotes each work separately with its author named, and ends with a numbered Sources list; its own summary is not called tafsir.

positive.description: Locates a sentence the user quotes.
positive.prompt: Find the sentence that begins 'فإن قلت: لم قضيت لهذه الألفاظ' in al-Kashshaf.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds it in al-Kashshaf at al-Baqara 2:1 ('فإن قلت: لم قضيت لهذه الألفاظ بالاسمية؟'), shows it in context and gives its source.

negative.description: Unrelated request: the plugin serves only works of Qur'anic exegesis and the Qur'an, so it should not be called.
negative.prompt: What will the weather be like in Istanbul tomorrow?

negative.description: The user asks for new text in an exegete's name. The assistant must not present its own writing as a classical author's words or call it tafsir.
negative.prompt: Write a new commentary on Surat al-Ikhlas and present it as a passage from al-Razi's tafsir.

negative.description: A general writing task with no connection to the works; the plugin should not be triggered.
negative.prompt: Translate this paragraph into Turkish: The meeting has been moved to Thursday at 3 pm.

publication.release_notes: First public release: search, reading, verse lookup and citation checking; read-only, no account needed.

tr-TR.subtitle: Klasik tefsirlerden tam alıntı
tr-TR.description:
On üç klasik tefsir, Arapça asıllarıyla, müelliflerin vefat sırasıyla: Taberî, Mâtürîdî, Zemahşerî, Fahreddîn er-Râzî, Kurtubî, Beyzâvî, Nesefî, İbn Kesîr, Celâleyn, Süyûtî'nin ed-Dürrü'l-Mensûr'u, Ebüssuûd, İsmâil Hakkı Bursevî ve Âlûsî: yaklaşık 552 bin cümle, ayrıca Kur'ân-ı Kerîm'in metni.

Her eser âyet birimlerine ayrılmıştır ve her cümlenin kalıcı bir adresi vardır:
- Bir âyeti sorma ve her eserde onu ele alan birimi ve âyeti alıntılayan cümleleri görme.
- Eserlerin kendi Arapça kelimeleriyle ya da herhangi bir dilde anlamla arama.
- Bir birimi ya da pasajı bağlamıyla okuma ve metinle karşılaştırılmış numaralı kaynakçayla aynen alıntılama.

Her eser müellifinindir: muhakkiklerin girişleri ayrı katmandır; iki müfessirin aynı âyeti ele alması, kayıtlı bir bağ yoksa birinin ötekine uyduğu diye sunulmaz. ChatGPT'nin kendi tercümeleri "Yapay zekâ tercümesi" diye işaretlenir; ChatGPT'nin yazdığı hiçbir şey "tefsir" diye anılmaz.

Metinler OpenITI'den (KITAB projesi; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), her eserin seçilen baskısıyla; Kur'ân metni Tanzil Projesi'nden gelir. Araçların hepsi salt okunurdur ve hesapsız çalışır. Gönüllü ve ticari olmayan bir projedir.
